findings.title: State-Changing Operation Executable via HTTP GET on /api/vulnerable/transfer
findings.evidence: HTTP GET triggered state mutation: {"success":true,"message":"Transferred $1 to audit_test (VULNERABLE: No CSRF token or origin check)","recipient":"audit_test","amount":1}
reproduction_steps: Notice endpoint executes transaction without requiring POST or CSRF validation
findings.impact: High. An attacker can execute arbitrary state changes by embedding the URL in a simple on a third-party webpage.
findings.remediation: Disallow GET on state-changing endpoints. Enforce POST/PUT with CSRF tokens.

findings.title: State-Changing POST Accepted Without CSRF Token on /api/vulnerable/transfer
findings.evidence: POST succeeded without X-CSRF-Token or CSRF form parameter: HTTP 200 OK
reproduction_steps: Send POST to http://localhost:3000/api/vulnerable/transfer with session cookie but omit CSRF token
findings.impact: Enables cross-origin sites to forge actions on behalf of authenticated users.
findings.remediation: Implement anti-CSRF token middleware (e.g., csrf-csrf or csurf) and require custom headers for API calls.

findings.title: Session Cookie Lacks SameSite Restriction on /api/vulnerable/transfer
reproduction_steps: Verify absence of SameSite=Lax or SameSite=Strict
findings.impact: Cookies are attached to cross-site requests, increasing vulnerability to CSRF.
findings.remediation: Configure SameSite=Lax or SameSite=Strict in cookie options: res.cookie(name, val, { sameSite: "lax", httpOnly: true, secure: true }).

findings.title: Anti-CSRF Token Enforced on /api/secure/transfer
findings.evidence: Request without token rejected with HTTP 403: {"error":"Forbidden: Missing or invalid CSRF token"}
findings.impact: Cross-site forgery prevented by anti-CSRF validation.
findings.remediation: Keep CSRF tokens required on all non-safe HTTP methods.
